preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 200000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(s) <= int(n) for n, m, s in [stdin.splitlines()[0].split()])
preconditions.description: The first line contains three integers n (number of cities), m (number of roads), and s (Bash's city), where 2 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5, 1 ≤ s ≤ n, and m is implicitly constrained by the input format.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in line.split()[:2]) and 1 <= int(line.split()[2]) <= 10**9 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the next m lines contains three integers u, v, w (1 ≤ u, v ≤ n, u ≠ v, 1 ≤ w ≤ 10^9) representing a bidirectional road between cities u and v with length w.
The input consists of exactly m + 1 lines: one for n, m, s and m lines for roads.

preconditions.expression: all(u != v for u, v, w in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself.

preconditions.expression: len({(u, v) for u, v, w in [(int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1]), int(line.split()[2])) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]}) == m
preconditions.description: There are no duplicate roads between the same pair of cities.

postconditions.description: The output is a single integer representing the maximum number of unhappy friends (0 ≤ answer ≤ n - 1).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.strip()) <= n - 1 and int(stdout.strip()) == max(unhappy_friends(city) for city in range(1, n + 1) if city != s))
postconditions.description: The output is the maximum number of unhappy friends when exactly one city (other than Bash's city s) is destroyed. A friend is unhappy if either: (1) their city is destroyed, or (2) their city is reachable from s before destruction but not after, or (3) the shortest path to their city increases after destruction.

The output is derived by evaluating the maximum number of unhappy friends across all possible cities to destroy (excluding Bash's city s). A friend is unhappy if their city is destroyed or their shortest path from s increases or becomes unreachable after destruction.
